temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Small, 4–5 oz 380°F / 195°C · 20 min 400°F / 205°C · 25 min Medium, 6–7 oz 380°F / 195°C · 24 min 400°F / 205°C · 30 min Large, 8 oz and over 380°F / 195°C · 28 min 400°F / 205°C · 35 min The thigh problem: rubbery skin, pink bone Thighs fail in two ways at once. The skin on top crisps quickly, but the fat under it needs time to render, so a thigh that looks done often has a rubbery layer under its crust. Meanwhile the meat closest to the bone is the last part to heat, and can still be pink when the outside is perfect. Starting skin side down solves most of it. With the skin against the basket, the fat renders slowly into the drawer while the meat cooks through; turning skin side up for the second half then crisps the now-thin skin in the direct air. Thighs are forgiving in one respect: dark meat stays moist well above the safe temperature, so a few extra minutes for the bone costs you almost nothing. Worked example Four medium bone-in thighs, around 6 oz each. Preheat 4 minutes, place them skin side down and cook at 380°F; turn them skin side up at 12 minutes and finish at 24 minutes. Larger thighs need about 28 minutes. In an oven-style air fryer the converter gives 380°F for 26 minutes. A conventional oven needs 400°F for around 30 minutes. How to tell they are done Measure next to the bone without touching it: 165°F (74°C) is safe, but thighs are at their best at 175–185°F, when the connective tissue has softened and the meat pulls cleanly from the bone. Juices should run clear when you pierce the thickest part. The skin should be deep golden and crisp all the way to the edges; if the edges are still soft, give them two more minutes skin side up. Before they go in Trim any large flaps of skin that hang over the sides, since they will burn before the rest is crisp. Dry the skin well and salt it; an hour uncovered in the fridge helps. No oil is needed on the skin side. If your thighs vary a lot in size, put the biggest pieces at the edges of the basket, where the air moves fastest. Related presets Chicken breast 375°F · 16 min · flip at 8 Chicken wings 400°F · 22 min · flip at 11 Chicken drumsticks 380°F · 22 min · flip at 11 400°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do bone-in chicken thighs take in the air fryer? About 24 minutes at 380°F for medium thighs, turned at 12 minutes. Small thighs take around 20 minutes, large ones around 28. What internal temperature should chicken thighs reach? 165°F (74°C) is the safe minimum. For tender thighs that come off the bone, aim for 175–185°F. Should I cook chicken thighs skin side up or down? Start skin side down to render the fat, then turn skin side up for the second half so the skin crisps in the direct air. Do boneless thighs take the same time? No, boneless thighs are thinner and cook faster, usually about the time in the small row of the table. Check the temperature early. What is the oven equivalent for chicken thighs? 400°F for around 30 minutes in a conventional oven, or 400°F for 27 minutes in a fan oven.
